(745mm.), in shaped travelling case (2) Letters and Certificate: A witnessed letter from Advocate Rudolf Lesky, Dresden, confirming the sale of the Violoncello to Julius Wegeler of Koblenz, dated 15th August 1879 and a receipt of the same date. Three letters from F. Ries to Julius Wegeler pertaining to the sale and dated 24th June, 27th June and 18th August 1879. (F. Ries was the dealer who acted for Wegeler in his negotiations with Kummer's executors). A letter from Phillip Hammig, Berlin, confirming the sale of the Violoncello to Delfim Ferreira, Oporto, dated 31st August 1937 and an associated receipt dated 25th October 1937. A certificate from Phillip Hammig, Berlin, dated 3rd September 1937. A letter from Joachim Hammig to Delfim Ferreira regarding the insurance of the Violoncello. All the above documents are collated in a book bound in Portuguese half morocco. Literature: William Henry, Arthur F. and Alfred E. Hill, The Violin Makers of the Guarneri Family p. 53 (the period of the instrument is erroneously referred to as 1730).  Friedrich August Kummer (born—Meiningen 1797—died—Dresden 1879) was regarded as the most accomplished 'cellist of his generation in Germany. He was well known as a composer, particularly for his own instrument. He also played the Oboe (See Colour Plate)
